title: bgmCompare
text: Compare graphical models between groups.

title: bgmCompare
text:
Description
bgmCompare() tests for differences in network structure between independent groups using Bayes factor tests.

title: bgmCompare
text:
Usage
bgmCompare(
  x,
  group,
  ...
)

title: bgmCompare
text:
Arguments



Argument
Description




x
A data frame or matrix of observations.


group
A factor or vector indicating group membership.


...
Additional arguments passed to the sampler.

title: bgmCompare
text:
Value
An object of class bgmCompare containing posterior samples and Bayes factors for group differences.

title: bgm
text: Bayesian estimation of graphical models for binary and/or ordinal variables.

title: bgm
text:
Description
bgm() fits a Bayesian graphical model using MCMC sampling. The model can handle ordinal variables (ordinal MRF) or continuous variables (Gaussian graphical model).

title: bgm
text:
Usage
bgm(
 x,
 variable_type = "ordinal",
 reference_category,
 iter = 10000,
 burnin = 1000,
 ...
)

title: bgm
text:
Arguments







Argument
Description




x
A data frame or matrix of observations.


variable_type
Character; "ordinal" (default) or "continuous".


reference_category
Reference category for ordinal variables.


iter
Number of MCMC iterations after burnin.


burnin
Number of burnin iterations.


...
Additional arguments (see documentation).

title: bgm
text:
Value
An object of class bgms containing:

interactions — Posterior samples for edge weights
thresholds — Posterior samples for threshold parameters

gamma — Edge inclusion indicators
prior — Prior specification used

title: bgm
text:
Examples

library(bgms)
data(Wenchuan)

# Basic usage
fit <- bgm(Wenchuan)
summary(fit)

# With edge selection
fit <- bgm(Wenchuan, edge_selection = TRUE)

title: bgm
text:
See Also
bgmCompare(), summary.bgms

text: This chapter covers installation and basic usage of bgms.

title: Getting Started
text:
Installation

From CRAN
install.packages("bgms")


Development Version
if(!requireNamespace("remotes")) {
  install.packages("remotes")
}
remotes::install_github("Bayesian-Graphical-Modelling-Lab/bgms")

title: Getting Started
text:
Basic Example
We’ll use the Wenchuan earthquake data included in the package:

library(bgms)

# Load example data
data(Wenchuan)

# Fit a Bayesian graphical model
fit <- bgm(Wenchuan)

# View results
summary(fit)

title: Getting Started
text:
Understanding the Output
The summary() output shows:

Edge inclusion probabilities — How likely is each edge to be present?
Parameter estimates — Posterior means for interaction strengths
Convergence diagnostics — ESS and R-hat values

title: C++ Architecture
text:
Overview
The bgms C++ backend is organized in three layers:








Layer
Location
Role




Algorithms
mcmc/algorithms/
Pure functions: nuts_step(), leapfrog()


Samplers
mcmc/samplers/
Stateful objects: NUTSSampler, HMCSampler


Runner
mcmc/execution/
MCMC loop orchestration

title: C++ Architecture
text:
Source Layout
src/
├── mcmc/
│   ├── algorithms/     # Stateless math
│   ├── samplers/       # Adaptation state
│   └── execution/      # Chain runner
├── models/
│   ├── base_model.h
│   ├── omrf/
│   └── ggm/
├── priors/
├── math/
└── utils/
